messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] hosted-runtime pool-7: kvcache OOM surge detected. alarm=KV_CACHE_OOM_RATE. severity=P1. @oncall-maya paged.
oncall-maya: Acknowledged. Observed customer impact? anyone seeing 5xx spikes?
eng-runtime-lee: Looking. Pod OOMs and restarts on pool-7 at 03:42 UTC. KV map jumped ~3x in 4m. Pushing logs.
eng-runtime-lee: ```
2026-04-02T03:42:12Z ERROR kvcache: oom allocating pages
kvmap/alloc.go:142 allocBulk() failed reserve 1.6GiB
runtime/prefetch.go:289 prefetchDepth=8200
```
sre-chris: Metrics: continuous_batch.window_median went from ~640 -> ~7680 at 03:41. GPU memory per pod peaked, host mem OK. Pattern looks like amplified prefixes (repeated long prompts).
prod-eng-ana: We deployed continuousBatch.min_window tweak to 0.75 in yesterday's rollout (canary passed quick smoke). Rolling that back now as emergency rollback.
oncall-maya: Before rollback, try applying temporary per-session prefetch cap (1024) and per-tenant soft limits. eng-runtime-lee can you patch runtime config?
eng-runtime-lee: Applying: `kubectl -n hosted exec runtime-pool-7 -- sh -c 'echo 1024 > /etc/runtime/kvcache/prefetch_cap'` and API push for tenant caps. Running now.
eng-runtime-lee: Also pushed tenant rule: `prefetch_cap_per_tenant=2048` and `new_session_token_limit=100000` to gateway. 200 OK.
sre-chris: After caps, KV allocation rate falling. Pod restarts slowing. Eviction rate still elevated but trending down. No new OOMs in last 4m.
support-jordan: CS: two customers reported transient 502s around 03:42-03:46 UTC on text-gen endpoints. I opened comms and asked if they need incident updates. No billing anomalies.
prod-eng-ana: Rollback started: helm rollback to continuousBatch.min_window=0.5 at 03:47 UTC. Monitoring rollout status.
oncall-maya: Good. Can we also pin a hard guard: if any single prefix consumes >25% of pool KV, auto-throttle that tenant to protect pool?
eng-runtime-lee: Created hotfix rule to throttle heavy-prefix tenants. Config: `prefix_share_threshold=0.25` -> action=throttle. Pushed to runtime control plane.
sre-chris: Grafana shows pool memory normalizing, traffic latency back to baseline. Marking mitigated at 03:51:00 UTC but keeping watch.
oncall-maya: I'll stay on until 04:30 UTC and then hand to night-sre. Please add follow-ups to incident file.
eng-runtime-lee: Follow-ups added: 1) Add prefetch amplification test in CI, 2) Lower default hosted prefetch_cap to 512, 3) Canary gating for continuousBatch changes (72h + traffic fuzzing), 4) Reach out to affected tenant (cust-omega) to discuss client patterns.
support-jordan: Drafting customer notification with timeline and mitigation steps.
incident-bot: Incident annotated: mitigated_by=runtime_caps+rollback+tenant_throttle. mitigation_time=2026-04-02T03:51:00Z.
oncall-maya: Thanks team. Creating postmortem channel and will include logs/metrics. :white_check_mark:
